_comment: Global delivery tuning, shared by generate.mts (character lane), generic.mts
(fallback quip bank) and wave_driver.sh (stamp signatures).
It lives in one file so that changing any of it invalidates the .voice stamps
and the affected takes get re-spoken. A constant buried in generate.mts would
not: the driver builds its signature from data, so a retune hidden in code
would leave every finished actor marked done in the old delivery.
Measured on this voice pool (3 takes per setting, king_bob + veil_ethan):
exaggeration 0.45 -> 0.75   pace +11%, pitch range +44%   <- the real knob
cfg_weight   0.55 -> 0.30   pace -12%, pitch range  +8%   <- backwards
exaggeration 0.85           pace  -3%, pitch range -32%   <- past the peak
Exaggeration is therefore the pace AND expression control, peaking near 0.75;
the folk wisdom that low cfg_weight speeds delivery is wrong for these
samples. Per-character exaggeration/cfgWeight live in characters.json.
tempo is an ffmpeg atempo stage applied after generation. The model's own
pacing is stochastic — the same settings gave +11% on one voice and +3% on
another — so the last few percent are bought deterministically instead. It is
pitch-preserving. Keep it under ~1.15; past that it starts to sound clipped
and artificial rather than brisk.
temperature is 0.8 deliberately. The service used to drop the field on the
non-streaming path, so every take — including all of the tuning measurements
above — actually ran at the library default of 0.8. The field is wired up now
(0.1 vs 1.5 measured an 18x spread in take-to-take variation), so this holds
it at the value the numbers above were gathered under. Lower it for steadier
reads, raise it for more variety between takes.
2026-08-16 pace retune (the reads were landing slow): exaggeration raised
0.70 -> 0.75, ONTO the measured pace peak — not past it, 0.85 is proven
slower and flatter. cfgWeight raised 0.55 -> 0.60, the top of the safe
0.50..0.62 band: the 0.55 -> 0.30 measurement shows lower reads SLOWER on
this pool, so within-band the anti-slow direction is up. The model's own
cadence does the work; tempo deliberately NOT raised (it is the atempo
speed ramp, and past ~1.15 it reads clipped rather than brisk). The recast
stripped every per-character knob, so these defaults now reach all 188
characters unshadowed, and touching this file re-stamps the whole pool.
